teaser: Merging devices, every call to the vault server named and opened, a page to browse your vaults, and one shared viewer that every reader vault opens with.
core_idea: The reader's vault became something a reader can see into and tidy: devices merge without losing a record, each call to the vault server is named and decrypted with keys the page already holds, a page walks every vault file by file and commit by commit, and one viewer, living in a vault of its own, is linked read-only into every reader vault as its app, the vault-in-vault technique proven in the live SG/App on a demo vault.

nodes.label: Five asks after Firefox
nodes.summary: The owner connected Firefox, found the workflow worked, and asked for merging, browsing, a shared viewer, readable calls and a clearer chooser.

nodes.label: Merge devices
nodes.summary: Several device files become one, every record re-filed and combined, the totals unchanged.

nodes.label: Aliases, not deletions
nodes.summary: activity/aliases.json sends a merged device's browser, files and inbox batches to the device it went into.

nodes.label: No payment lost
nodes.summary: A top-up is a payment record; a merge moves it and never drops it.

nodes.label: A chooser that names the destination
nodes.summary: The likely device first, a button that says where the browser goes, and Change to move it later.

nodes.label: The Calls tab
nodes.summary: Every call named from its address, and opened into a commit, tree, ref or file with the vault's own key.

nodes.label: Your vaults, opened
nodes.summary: A page that opens the four vaults of an account and shows files, contents and commits, writing nothing.

nodes.label: sgit.ai's sub-vaults
nodes.summary: A link file with no key, the read key in an owner record, and app reads spliced through the link.

nodes.label: Four files in the reader vault
nodes.summary: The link, the owner record, the app manifest and a short entry page, written on the next Update.

nodes.label: One shared viewer
nodes.summary: The viewer lives once, in vault lkypj6zq, and every reader vault that links it shows its new versions.

nodes.label: Proven in the live SG/App
nodes.summary: A demo reader vault linked the same way opened read-only and rendered through the viewer.

nodes.label: Only a read key leaves
nodes.summary: The SG/Vault app is handed the reader vault's read key over its embed protocol, and the test checks it is nothing else.

nodes.label: Undo and deep links
nodes.summary: Splitting a merged device and opening the app straight onto its history are not built.

quotes.text: Merging keeps every record and every payment, moves them into one device file, and leaves an alias so a browser still using a merged device lands in the right place.
quotes.why: the rule of a merge, and the reason it is safe for money
the whole of the vault-in-vault technique in five words

figures.caption: A demo reader vault opened in the SG/App at dev.vault.sgraph.ai, read-only, from its published read key. The page is the newsroom's viewer: its code came from a different vault, lkypj6zq, through a link file, and it drew the account from the demo vault's own records, a balance of £4.84, three pages read, two notes, two devices. The badge at the top right says the session cannot write.

The Vault tab in the pane, 400 pixels wide, in Newsprint, with two devices ticked in Across your devices. The bar under the table offers to merge them into one of the two, under a name that can be changed, and says that nothing is deleted. The total row is the account recomputed from the records.

The Calls tab, widened, after an update of the reader vault. One batch call is open: inside it, a file's contents (the entry page the update wrote), a tree with six entries, a commit with its message, time, tree and parent, and a ref pointing at that commit. Each was decrypted in the page with the reader vault's key; the server holds only the ciphertext.

The page Your vaults, opened, after a merge: the reader vault's tree on the left, the merged device's file in the middle with the device it was merged from in its header, and the commits on the right, newest first, from the merge back to the vault's creation. Picking a commit shows the tree and the files as they were then.

How the viewer is linked. Left, a reader vault: its records under activity/, and four small files the next Update writes. Right, the newsroom's viewer in vault lkypj6zq, with its code. Below, what the SG/App does when it opens the reader vault: reads the manifest, opens the viewer vault read-only from the owner record, loads the viewer's code through the link, and lets it read the reader's own records.
